'''Stanley Johnson Jr.''' (born May 29, 1996) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]], and earned [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-American|All-American]] honors in his freshman year. After the season, he declared himself eligible for the [[2015 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining three years of college eligibility.

Johnson was one of the top high school recruits of 2014 by Rivals.com, Scout.com and ESPN. He was a four-time [[California Interscholastic Federation|CIF]] State champion. He completed his senior season for [[Mater Dei High School]] during the 2013–14 season. A native of [[Fullerton, California]]. He played in the 2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game, 2014 Jordan Brand Classic and the 2014 Nike Hoop Summit. He was a 2014 USA Today first team All-USA Boys Basketball Team selection. Arguably the best player to ever play in Orange County, he won 4 straight State Championships at Mater Dei.

==High school career==
Johnson was born in [[Anaheim, California]], to Karen Taylor and Stanley Johnson Sr. His parents divorced and his father remarried. Johnson was the couple's only child, and he was raised by his mother in [[Fullerton, California|Fullerton]].<ref name=sondheimer_03152014>{{cite news|last=Sondheimer|first=Eric|title=Mater Dei's Stanley Johnson Jr. goes full-throttle on basketball court|date=March 15, 2014|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://articles.latimes.com/print/2014/mar/15/sports/la-sp-stanley-johnson-mater-dei-20140316|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6Y0WI5HBg|archivedate=April 23, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref> His mother played college basketball at [[Jackson State Lady Tigers basketball|Jackson State]], who inducted her into their Sports Hall of Fame in 2009, and played professionally in Europe.<ref name=sondheimer_03152014/><ref name=u18_profile>{{cite web|title=Stanley Johnson|publisher=USA Basketball|url=http://archive.usab.com/bios/johnson_stanley.html|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6Y0YhJEGF|archivedate=April 23, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref> Johnson attended Mater Dei High School in 2010 and graduated May 31, 2014, where he started on the varsity basketball team for four years and won four CIF California Division I basketball championships in his four seasons. He played and defended all five positions in high school.

===Freshman===
As a freshman in 2010-11, along with 2011-12 USA Developmental National Team member Shaqquan Aaron, aided the Monarchs to the 2011 CIF California Division I championship and a 32-3 record.

===Sophomore===
Pulled down 15 rebounds in the 2012 state championship game, where in 2011-12 he helped lead his team to its second-straight CIF Division I state title, a 33-2 mark and a No. 7 final national ranking by USA Today; started all 35 games and averaged 16.0 ppg., 8.0 rpg., 2.0 apg. and 3.0 spg.

===Junior===
Where in 2012-13 he helped lead his team to its third-straight CIF Division I state title, a 35-0 mark and a No. 1 final national ranking by USA Today; started all 35 games and averaged 18.0 ppg., 8.0 rpg., 2.0 apg. and 3.0 spg.

===Senior===
Where in 2013-14 he helped lead his team to its fourth-straight CIF Division I state title, a 35-0 mark and a No. 1 final national ranking by USA Today; started all 35 games and averaged 25.0 ppg., 8.0 rpg., 2.0 apg. and 3.0 spg.

==University of Arizona==
Johnson committed to Arizona on November 15, 2013. Johnson made his debut Sunday November 9, 2014 4:00 p.m. PST on [[Pac-12 Network]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.arizonawildcats.com/SportSelect.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30700&SPID=127128&SPSID=750089&DB_OEM_ID=30700 |title=Men's Basketball - Schedule - The University of Arizona Official Athletic Site |publisher=Arizonawildcats.com |date= |accessdate=2015-03-28}}</ref> As a freshman in 2014–15, Johnson was voted first-team [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]], and was named Pac-12 Freshman of the Year.<ref>{{cite press release|title=2014-15 Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Honors|date=March 9, 2015|publisher=Pac-12|url=http://pac-12.com/article/2015/03/09/2014-15-pac-12-conference-mens-basketball-honors|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6WuCA8C5K|archivedate=March 9, 2015|deadurl=no}}</ref> Stanley and the Wildcats were eliminated in the Elite Eight by the Wisconsin Badgers by the score of 85-78.

==NBA==
On April 23, 2015, Johnson announced that he would declare for the 2015 NBA Draft.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Feldman|first1=Dan|title=Arizona’s Stanley Johnson, last probable lottery pick to declare, headed to NBA draft|url=http://probasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2015/04/24/arizonas-stanley-johnson-last-probable-lottery-pick-to-declare-headed-to-nba-draft/|website=NBC Sports|accessdate=25 April 2015}}</ref> He enters as the 11th ranked prospect on ESPN's Top 100 draft board. <ref>{{cite web|last1=Ford|first1=Chad|title=Chad Ford's Top 100|url=http://insider.espn.go.com/nba/draft/results/top100/_/year/2015|website=ESPN|accessdate=25 April 2015}}</ref>

==International play==
Johnson earned gold medals in the 2011 [[FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship]], [[2012 FIBA Under-17 World Championship]] and [[2014 FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]]. Johnson served as [[captain (sports)|captain]] 2014 team and earned MVP of the 2014 tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.usab.com/mens/u18/14_mu18_game_05.html|title=USA Basketball Men’s U18 National Team Claims 2014 FIBA Americas U18 Championship Gold Medal With 113-79 Victory Over Canada|accessdate=2014-06-25|date=2014-06-24|publisher=[[USA Basketball]]}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Johnson is the stepson of Easter Johnson. The youngest of five children, he has two brothers and two sisters.<ref name=u18_profile/>
